alignments.note: The attributive demonstrative supplies the determiner, so the article realizes nothing, rule 38.
The italicized *but* is an intensifying helper on the numeral, rule 7; rule 11 keeps the italics from making it added. Marking it added under rule 5 remains defensible.

Case preposition rides with the pronoun, rule 21's determinerless clause. This pronoun is also the antecedent the following relative clause is predicated of, so it is spent for that purpose under rule 32.

The article's phrase stands in apposition to the expressed ἡμῖν, which has already written the antecedent pronoun, so nothing is left for the article to supply: rule 32's apposition clause, whose own example `τοῖς δὲ σῳζομένοις ἡμῖν` → *unto us who are saved* is this same dative frame. Rule 76's availability test does not reach it, an antecedent being the very word the relative clause is predicated of. Rule 90 is the near contrast and does not apply, the ASV having written both an antecedent word and a relativizer for this phrase.
The participle keeps the supplied relativizer along with its own verb and auxiliary, rule 32's apposition clause, headed on the lexical verb under rule 17.
Case preposition rides with the article that carries the determiner, rule 21.
One Greek noun rendered by an adjective-plus-noun phrase whose noun glosses the lexeme, rule 66.

review_notes: Corrected: the accepted alignment gave *who* to s013 under rule 90, but rule 90 governs only a phrase for which the ASV writes a single double-duty word serving as pronoun and relativizer at once. Here the ASV writes an antecedent (*us*) and a relativizer (*who*) separately, and the antecedent is written by the expressed ἡμῖν, which the article's phrase stands in apposition to.

Rule 32's apposition clause therefore empties the article and gives *who have borne* to the participle, headed on *borne* — the identical reading it records for `τοῖς δὲ σῳζομένοις ἡμῖν` → *unto us who are saved*.
A reference comparison will report the unrepresented s013 as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction, as rule 32 says in terms.
The italicized *but* on μίαν is left folded as a rule 7 helper on the numeral; the competing added reading is named in the unit's note.
